They say that scratching a programmer's itch kick starts an open source project. However, we all know that the itch can take us only so far. Sooner or later, it is the community that needs to get around a FOSS project in order to keep the flame alive. Only when users try out a product, beta testers start raising the issues, documenters start writing good documentation, do devs like me feel inspired to scratch that forgotten itch again.

We all know that there are many side-projects which begin life on github with many stars and then just wither away due to lack of users and finally, the devs too stop taking interest.

Few months ago, I went through the same cycle when I started a side-project Visual Alchemist. It began its life as a humble tool to quickly draw a few database tables on a bootstrap-frontend canvas and export it as python-SQLAlchemy ORM code. I was working extensively on Python at that time, hence I started that project. As usual, the project just withered away after some time, but recently I've taken a renewed interest in its development again. This time, I don't have any particular interest in Python, but I want to start making VA a generic tool that outputs to multiple formats apart from python-sqlalchemy. Things on the feature-map include raw sql formats (mysql, postresql, etc.) and other ORMs such as the PHP doctrine. In other words, I want to establish a community around VA and want to spread its usefulness to as many people across the word as possible! I want to transform my own insignificant itch into a community itch that keeps getting treated and the software gets evolved and better with each iteration.

Of course, thats my whole idea. Its even possible that I'll find no public interest in VA despite my best efforts, but I'm prepared for that too. This time, I'm expecting that as a possibility, so I won't just ignore this project even if that happens.

So, I invite you all to collaborate in this project of mine. The people I need most right now are users, beta-testers and document writers. Agreed that this is a very small sized app at the moment, compared to many other large FOSS projects. However, there are some innovative things planned in the featuremap for v2.0. There is no Linus Torvalds or rms backing this project, but I can assure you of one thing: there will always be at least one developer working on this project and that will be me!

These are a few things I've done until now to show my commitment towards VA project:

  1. Refactored the old code, and added raw mysql as an output format.
  2. Changed the license from MIT to GNU GPLv3 to demonstrate my commitment towards this project.
  3. Updated the project README.md file with all project details such as governance style (meritocracy) and contact details.
  4. Created /v/VisualAlchemist as a discussion room to discuss improvements in VA.
  5. Using my hilariously limited GIMP skills, even created a logo for the project (crude I know, but at least something is better than nothing!).
  6. Created a hosted version of VA for a live demo that users can use!
  7. Defined the feature maps, so the project can have some vision about what to develop in the near term. Release 1.1 is mostly about adding a plethora of additional output formats (postgresql, sqlite, doctrine, maybe others). Release 2.0 is about the enhancements like adding charting features, integration with actual backend orms and automate them and a few aesthetic features. Of course, you may have many more ideas to make VA better apart from these, I welcome you to discuss them on /v/VisualAlchemist!
